text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- King Hussein and Palestinian leader Arafat, in a phone call over the latest peace developments, stress the need to constantly coordinate over Arab East Jerusalem's holy sites. They emphasise the city's Arab and Islamic character.
- King Hussein cancels the traditional Moslem Eid al-Fitr reception to receive well-wishers on medical advice not to exhaust himself after a recent knee surgery.

- Crown Prince heads to London on a private visit which will be followed next Tuesday by official talks in Paris with French leaders on the "rehabilitation of the Middle East and ongoing Jordan-EU talks over a partnership accord."
- Prime Minister opens a major traffic intersection in the capital; heeps praise on the municipality's efforts to ease traffic bottlenecks.
- Cabinet approves new allowances for doctors in the state medical sector, ending a long simmering pay dispute.

- Crown Prince and Prime Minister meet British Foreign Secretary Rifkind's special envoy who is visiting the region; Jordan says the proposed Organisation for Cooperation in the Middle East (OCME) could be a framework to discuss regional issues of common interest such as water, environment, and energy.
